title: Testing: unit, API and integration tests
seriesDescription: Topic-by-topic JEE-style quizzes for the backend and AI-engineering interview roadmap: integer, assertion-reason, matrix match, fill-in-the-blanks, short code writing, plus multi-correct questions. Language core, concurrency, DSA, web frameworks, data access, databases, messaging, resilience, security, testing, system design, LLM and agent engineering.
description: JUnit 5 and Mockito, pytest fixtures and unittest.mock, MockMvc, TestClient, @DataJpaTest, Testcontainers, test-case design with boundaries, edge cases and contract tests.
source: JUnit 5 user guide; Mockito docs; Spring Boot testing reference; pytest docs; Python unittest.mock docs; FastAPI testing docs; Testcontainers docs; Pact docs

questions.prompt: Write a JUnit 5 test method for PriceService (it has a PriceRepo repo field) that stubs repo.find("A") to return 10, calls svc.price("A"), asserts the result is 10 and verifies that repo.find("A") was called once. Assume repo is a Mockito mock and svc is already built.
questions.explanation: Annotate the class with @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class) and use @Mock / @InjectMocks. BDDMockito given(...).willReturn(...) and AssertJ assertThat are equally valid.

questions.prompt: Write a MockMvc call that GETs /api/orders/42, expects HTTP 200 and expects the JSON field id to equal 42. Assume a MockMvc named mockMvc.
questions.explanation: @WebMvcTest(OrderController.class) with a @MockBean/@MockitoBean service gives a fast web-layer test. perform throws Exception, so the test method declares throws Exception.

questions.prompt: Write a pytest function test_get_item using FastAPI's TestClient on app that requests /items/1, asserts a 200 status code and asserts the JSON id is 1.
questions.model:
def test_get_item():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/items/1")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json()["id"] == 1
questions.explanation: No server is started: TestClient calls the ASGI app in-process. Use httpx.AsyncClient with ASGITransport for async tests, and app.dependency_overrides to swap the database dependency.

questions.prompt: A function-scoped fixture db is requested by four plain tests and by one test parametrised with three values. How many times does the fixture run in a full session?
questions.explanation: Function scope sets up once per test invocation: 4 plain tests plus 3 parametrised cases make 7. With scope="module" it would run once.

questions.prompt: A form accepts ages from 18 to 65 inclusive. How many test inputs does classic two-value boundary value analysis use (one just outside and one on each boundary)?
questions.explanation: The values are 17, 18, 65 and 66: the two boundaries plus the neighbour just outside each. Add a typical value in the middle for the equivalence class if you want.

questions.prompt: app/service.py does "import requests" and calls requests.get(...). Which unittest.mock target replaces it for a test of service.py?

options.why: Right: patch the name where the code under test looks it up.

options.text: patch("requests.get") globally inside a conftest.py fixture only
options.why: It can work by luck, but the rule is to patch the lookup site, not rely on global side effects.
The test module is not where service.py reads the name.

questions.explanation: Where to patch: for "from requests import get" you must patch app.service.get instead. Use autospec=True to make the mock honour the real signature.

questions.prompt: Match each Spring test annotation or library to what it provides.

right.text: Controller slice with MockMvc and no service beans
JPA slice with an embedded database and rollback after each test
A real database in Docker started for the test
A mock web server for outgoing HTTP

questions.explanation: Slices load only part of the context for speed. Use Testcontainers when H2 differs from production (jsonb, partial indexes, locking behaviour).

questions.prompt: Read the assertion and the reason, then choose the option that describes them correctly.
questions.assertion: @DataJpaTest tests roll back their changes by default.
questions.reason: Each @DataJpaTest test runs inside a transaction that Spring rolls back when the test ends.

whys.a: Right: the transactional test is the mechanism.

questions.explanation: Remember that rollback also hides flush-time constraint errors; call flush() or entityManager.flush() when you want them to surface.

questions.prompt: Read the assertion and the reason, then choose the option that describes them correctly.
questions.assertion: Mocking collaborators makes a unit test fast and isolated.
questions.reason: Since Mockito 5 the inline mock maker is the default, so final classes can be mocked.

whys.a: The final-class fact does not explain speed or isolation.
whys.b: Right: both are true but independent.

questions.explanation: Do not mock types you do not own or simple value objects; wrap them in an adapter you control instead.

questions.prompt: Read the assertion and the reason, then choose the option that describes them correctly.
questions.reason: @SpringBootTest always opens a real HTTP server on port 8080.

whys.c: Right: the default webEnvironment is MOCK, and RANDOM_PORT must be requested explicitly.
whys.d: The assertion is the true statement.

questions.explanation: Use webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT with TestRestTemplate or WebTestClient when you need a real server.

questions.prompt: Read the assertion and the reason, then choose the option that describes them correctly.
questions.assertion: To isolate a class in a unit test you should mock the class under test itself.
questions.reason: Mocks replace collaborators with controllable stand-ins.

whys.d: Right: mocking the class under test removes the very code you want to test; the reason is true.

questions.explanation: Mock the dependencies of the class under test. Use a spy only when you must partially stub a real object.

questions.text: A consumer-driven {1} test (for example Pact) checks that a provider still honours what consumers rely on, without a full {2} environment, while tests of a pure function with plain inputs are {3} tests.
questions.explanation: Contract tests catch breaking API changes early, which is what makes independent deployment of services safe.

questions.prompt: A function parseDate("dd/mm/yyyy") returns a LocalDate. Which inputs are worthwhile edge cases? Select all that apply.

options.why: Right: leap-year logic is a classic edge.
Right: error handling on missing input.
It repeats the happy path and adds little.

questions.explanation: Edge cases come from boundaries, invalid input, empty values and special calendars.

questions.prompt: A test passes alone but fails in the full suite, and also fails near midnight. What is the most reliable cure for the time-related failure?

options.text: Inject a Clock (or freeze time) so the test controls "now"
options.why: Right: time becomes an input, not an ambient dependency.

options.text: Add Thread.sleep(2000) before the assertion so the clock ticks over
options.why: Sleeping makes tests slow and still flaky.

options.text: Retry the test up to five times in the CI config
Run the suite only during the daytime
options.why: Scheduling around the bug does not fix it.

questions.explanation: Flaky causes: shared state, ordering, time, randomness, concurrency and real network calls. Isolate each by injecting or seeding it.

questions.prompt: Using different @MockBean (or @MockitoBean) sets in different test classes can force Spring to build additional application contexts.

options.why: Right: the cache key includes the mock definitions, so each distinct set creates a new context.
The Spring TestContext cache is keyed by configuration, and mock beans are part of that configuration.

questions.explanation: To keep builds fast, share a base test configuration and avoid scattering @MockBean over many classes.
